title: Electric field magnitude
description: Essential: Correctly states the final answer for part (1) as E = v₀B.

title: Work-energy application
description: Important: Applies the work-energy theorem to relate electric potential energy change to kinetic energy change for part (2).

title: Vertical coordinate y₁
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the final numerical expression for part (2): y₁ = 3mv₀/(32eB).

title: Force balance at extremes
description: Important: Analyzes the net Lorentz force (electric and magnetic) at the highest and lowest points of the trajectory.

title: Maximum height condition
description: Important: Derives the expression for the maximum vertical coordinate y in terms of initial velocity v.

title: Velocity threshold inequality
description: Important: Sets up and solves the inequality y(v) ≥ y₂ to find the minimum initial velocity required to reach y₂.

title: Percentage calculation
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the final percentage for part (3) as 90%.

title: Sign error in Lorentz force
description: Pitfall: Uses an incorrect sign for the magnetic force component, leading to wrong force balance or trajectory analysis.

title: Misapplied work-energy theorem
description: Pitfall: Incorrectly equates work done by the electric field to the total kinetic energy change without accounting for the correct initial/final states.

title: Unit or constant omission
description: Optional: Includes proper units in final answers or explicitly notes the charge magnitude 'e'.
